en: to build; to construct; to build anew

examples.ko: 시는 낡은 도서관을 허물고 그 자리에 신축했어요.
examples.en: The city tore down the old library and built a new one on the spot.

examples.ko: 회사가 내년에 본사 건물을 신축할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will construct a new headquarters building next year.

examples.ko: 건물을 신축하는 공사가 한 달째 이어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The construction of the new building has been going on for a month.
They built a new school, so the classrooms got much bigger.

examples.ko: 아파트를 신축하고 나면 이름이 바뀔 수도 있어요.
examples.en: After the new apartment is built, its name might change.

examples.ko: 집을 신축하려면 먼저 허가를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To build a new house, you need to get a permit first.

explain: 건물을 새로 지을 때 써요. 일상에서는 '짓다'를 많이 쓰고, 신축하다는 공사, 부동산, 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 있는 건물에 더하는 일은 '증축', 헐고 다시 짓는 일은 '개축'이라고 구분해요.

phrases.en: They built a new library next to the city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고, 일상 대화에서는 '신축하다'보다 '새로 짓다'를 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, and in daily conversation '새로 짓다' is used more than '신축하다'.

phrases.en: This is a newly built building from last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 지은 건물을 가리킬 때 쓰는 짝말이에요. 부동산 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for a newly constructed building, often heard in real estate talk.

phrases.example: 학교 옆에서 신축 공사를 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: New construction is going on next to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 건물을 짓는 공사를 말해요. 증축 공사와 구분해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Construction of a new building, distinguished from extension work.

explain_en: Building a brand-new building, real estate and construction term. Use it for constructing a building new. Everyday speech uses '짓다', while 신축하다 appears in construction, real estate and the news. Adding onto an existing building is '증축', and tearing down and rebuilding is '개축'.

gh: build big works like roads or bridges
create land, a park, or a complex
everyday native verb: make a house
build and found, like a school or monument
build stone or earth structures, like walls

p.n: 건축하다 doesn't say that the building is new.

t90.ax: To build a new house, you need to get a permit first.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 아버지가 남겨 주신 애장품이에요.
examples.en: This watch is a treasured item my father left me.

examples.ko: 제 애장품 1호는 어릴 때 받은 곰 인형이에요.
examples.en: My number one treasured item is a teddy bear I got as a child.
The museum is exhibiting a famous writer's treasured belongings.
The singer put her prized belongings up for auction.
I store my treasured item carefully in case it gets damaged.

examples.ko: 만화책은 제 소중한 애장품 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Comic books are one of my precious belongings.

explain: 내가 특별히 아끼는 물건을 말해요. '소장품'은 모아서 가지고 있는 물건이고, '애장품'은 아끼는 마음이 더 들어간 말이에요.

phrases.en: He introduced his treasured items on the show.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아끼는 물건을 보여 주며 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing and talking about cherished items.

phrases.example: 그 책을 평생 애장품으로 간직하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've kept that book as a treasure all my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 소중히 보관한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping something dear for a long time.

phrases.en: This is the item I cherish most.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애장품'을 쉽게 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way of saying 'aejangpum'.

explain_en: It refers to an item you particularly cherish. '소장품' is something you own in a collection, while '애장품' carries more of a feeling of affection.

examples.en: There is a mother-of-pearl wardrobe in my grandmother's room.
This mirror's frame is decorated with mother-of-pearl.

examples.ko: 자개가 빛에 따라 색이 다르게 보여요.
examples.en: The mother-of-pearl looks like a different color depending on the light.
I received a small mother-of-pearl table as a gift.
Mother-of-pearl wardrobes are still regarded as high-end furniture.

examples.ko: 전통 공예 박물관에서 자개 작품을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I looked at mother-of-pearl works at the traditional craft museum.

explain: 조개껍데기 안쪽의 반짝이는 부분을 얇게 잘라 가구나 상자에 붙여 꾸밀 때 쓰는 재료예요. '자개장', '자개상'처럼 가구 이름 앞에 붙여 많이 말하고, 이런 공예를 '나전칠기'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My maternal grandmother's house has an old mother-of-pearl wardrobe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자개로 꾸민 장롱을 줄여서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short name for a wardrobe decorated with mother-of-pearl.

phrases.en: On holidays we set the food out on a mother-of-pearl table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자개로 꾸민 작은 상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a small table decorated with mother-of-pearl.

phrases.en: I tried mother-of-pearl crafting at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자개로 물건을 만들고 꾸미는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the craft of making and decorating things with mother-of-pearl.

explain_en: It is the shiny inner part of a shell, cut thin and attached to furniture or boxes as decoration. It is often placed before furniture names such as 자개장 and 자개상, and this craft is also called 나전칠기.

examples.ko: 새 다리를 올해 말에 준공할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The new bridge is scheduled to be completed at the end of this year.
The company completed construction of a new factory.

examples.ko: 시청이 새 도서관을 준공해서 시민들이 기뻐해요.
examples.en: City Hall finished building the new library, and citizens are happy.

examples.ko: 건물을 준공하려면 안전 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To complete a building, you must pass a safety inspection.

examples.ko: 아파트를 준공하고 나서 바로 입주가 시작됐어요.
examples.en: Move-in began right after the apartment complex was completed.

examples.ko: 터널을 준공하는 날에 큰 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: A big event is held on the day the tunnel is completed.

explain: 건물, 다리, 도로 같은 큰 공사가 끝났을 때 써요. 작은 일에는 안 쓰고 '끝내다', '마치다'를 써요. 공사를 시작하는 건 '착공하다'예요. 뉴스에서는 '준공식', '준공 검사'로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: There is a completion ceremony for the new bridge tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 공사가 끝났음을 알리는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a ceremony marking the end of a big construction project.

phrases.en: The new building will be completed next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이나 도로를 주어로 해서 공사가 끝난다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Takes a building or road as subject to say construction finishes.

phrases.example: 이 도로 공사를 올해 안에 마칠 거예요.
phrases.en: We will finish this road construction within this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '준공하다' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday alternative to '준공하다'.

explain_en: Official term, used by city or government for finished construction (도서관 준공) Use it when a large construction project, like a building, bridge, or road, is finished. For small things say '끝내다' or '마치다'. Starting construction is '착공하다'. In the news it also appears as '준공식' and '준공 검사'.

gh: finish a program, without earning a degree

p.n: 완성하다 is generic; 준공하다 is the official construction term.

t90.ax: The company completed construction of a new factory.

examples.en: I saw a mirror made of bronze at the museum.

examples.ko: 광장 한가운데에 청동 동상이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A bronze statue stands in the middle of the square.
Bronze is made by mixing copper and tin.
A bronze knife was found in the tomb.

examples.ko: 이 종은 청동이라서 소리가 오래 울려요.
examples.en: This bell is bronze, so the sound rings for a long time.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁에는 오래된 청동 그릇이 있어요.
examples.en: My grandmother's house has an old bronze bowl.

explain: 올림픽 3등 상은 '동메달'이라고 하고 '청동 메달'이라고는 잘 안 해요. 청동은 '청동기 시대', '청동 거울', '청동상'처럼 역사 이야기와 유물·조각 이름에 주로 써요.

phrases.example: 청동기 시대 사람들은 청동으로 도구를 만들었어요.
phrases.en: People in the Bronze Age made tools from bronze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 시대 이름이라서 역사 이야기에서 가장 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A historical era name, most common in history talk.

phrases.en: There is a big bronze statue in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청동으로 만든 조각이나 동상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A statue or sculpture made of bronze.

phrases.en: I saw old bronze artifacts at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날에 청동으로 만든 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for ancient objects made of bronze.

explain_en: For the Olympic third place, people say 동메달, not 청동 메달. 청동 mostly appears in history topics and names of relics and statues, such as 청동기 시대, 청동 거울, and 청동상.

examples.en: The city announced it will develop new housing land.

examples.ko: 이 택지는 학교와 공원이 가까워서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This housing area is popular because schools and parks are close.

examples.ko: 택지 가격이 올라서 집값도 같이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Land prices went up, and house prices rose along with them.
Apartments are planned to be built on the new town's housing land.
I live in a neighborhood that was developed as housing land.

examples.ko: 주변 택지 분양 일정을 확인하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm checking the sale schedule for housing lots nearby.

explain: 집을 짓기 위한 땅을 말해서 일반적인 '땅'이나 '토지'보다 좁아요. '택지 개발', '택지 분양'처럼 부동산 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 농사짓는 땅은 '농지'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 새 아파트 택지 분양이 다음 달에 시작돼요.
phrases.en: The sale of the new apartment lots starts next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 지을 땅을 나눠 파는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for dividing up and selling land for building houses.

phrases.en: A school and a park will be built in the new housing development district.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 지으려고 정한 넓은 지역을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a wide area designated for building houses.

phrases.example: 그는 시골에 택지를 사서 집을 지었어요.
phrases.en: He bought a housing lot in the countryside and built a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 지을 땅을 산다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying someone bought land to build a house on.

explain_en: Land prepared for building homes or apartments. It is land meant for building houses, so it is narrower than the general words '땅' or '토지'. It often appears in real-estate news as '택지 개발' or '택지 분양', while farmland is called '농지'.

examples.ko: 파스텔 색 원피스가 봄에 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: A pastel-colored dress suits spring well.
The child drew the sky with pastels.
I decorated the room in pastel tones.
If you rub pastel with your hand, the color smears.
I like a soft pastel pink for the wallpaper.
Pastels were expensive, so I only bought twenty colors.

explain: 그림 도구 이름이기도 하고 '파스텔 톤'처럼 연하고 부드러운 색을 가리키기도 해요. 옷, 인테리어, 화장품에서 '파스텔 톤', '파스텔 컬러'가 아주 자주 나와요. 진하고 선명한 색은 '비비드'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Decorating the room in pastel tones makes it feel comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연하고 부드러운 색의 분위기를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to describe a light, soft color mood.

phrases.en: Pastel-colored bags are popular this spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 패션 기사나 쇼핑에서 파스텔 톤과 비슷하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much like 파스텔 톤 in fashion articles and shopping.

phrases.en: I draw flower pictures with pastels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림 도구로 쓰일 때의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing for when it means the drawing tool.

explain_en: It is the name of a drawing tool, and it also refers to light, soft colors, as in '파스텔 톤'. '파스텔 톤' and '파스텔 컬러' show up constantly in clothes, interior design and cosmetics. Strong, vivid colors are called '비비드'.

en: to reclaim; to cultivate; to clear land

examples.en: My grandfather cleared the foot of the mountain and made a field.
To clear wasteland, you have to pick out the stones first.

examples.ko: 사람들이 갯벌을 개간하는 일에 대해 이야기했어요.
examples.en: People talked about reclaiming the tidal flats.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 십 년 동안 땅을 개간했어요.
examples.en: Our family cleared the land for ten years.
Clearing a forest affects the environment.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 함께 벌판을 개간하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The villagers began clearing the field together.

explain: 주로 '땅을 개간하다', '황무지를 개간하다'처럼 목적어에 땅이나 들판이 와요. 새 길이나 분야를 여는 일에는 '개척하다'를 쓰니까 구별해서 써요.

phrases.en: This is land my grandfather reclaimed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개간한 + 명사' 형태로 어떤 땅인지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '개간한 + noun' form describes what kind of land it is.

phrases.en: They cleared the mountain and made a field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개간한 결과 무엇이 되었는지 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to continue and say what it became after clearing.
phrases.en_equiv: to clear and make a field

phrases.example: 요즘 마을 사람들이 숲을 개간하고 있어요.
phrases.en: These days the villagers are clearing the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something in progress.

explain_en: Turning wild land into fields. The object is usually land, as in '땅을 개간하다' or '황무지를 개간하다'. For opening up a new path or field, use '개척하다' instead.

t90.ax: Our family cleared the land for ten years.

examples.en: I looked at the place where the sky and sea meet.

examples.ko: 두 집의 담이 서로 맞닿아 있어요.
examples.en: The walls of the two houses touch each other.
My heart raced the moment our fingertips touched.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 옆집 벽과 맞닿고 있어서 소리가 잘 들려요.
examples.en: Our room shares a wall with the next house, so sounds carry easily.
Cups make a sound when they touch each other.

examples.ko: 책상 두 개를 맞닿을 만큼 가깝게 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put two desks so close that they touch.

explain: 둘이 서로 끝이 닿을 때 써서 '서로 맞닿다'처럼 자주 말해요. 한쪽이 상대에게 닿는 건 '닿다', 아예 붙어 버린 건 '붙다'를 써요. 소리는 [맏따타]로 나요.

phrases.en: The two palms touched each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'와 함께 써서 둘이 마주 닿는다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '서로', it is clear that both sides touch.

phrases.en: My house borders the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 닿은 상태가 계속될 때 '-아 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아 있다' for a state of staying in contact.

phrases.example: 두 판이 맞닿은 부분에 틈이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a gap where the two boards meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 닿은 곳을 가리킬 때 '맞닿은 + 명사'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '맞닿은 + noun' to point to where two things meet.

explain_en: It is used when two things touch end to end, so '서로 맞닿다' (touch each other) is a common phrase. When only one side reaches the other, use '닿다'; when they are completely stuck together, use '붙다'. It is pronounced [맏따타].

examples.en: I worked at one workplace for half of my life.
My father has done nothing but farm for half of his life.

examples.ko: 반평생이 지나서야 제 꿈을 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: Only after half my life had passed did I realize what my dream was.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 우리 가족이 반평생 지켜 온 곳이에요.
examples.en: This shop is a place our family has kept going for half a lifetime.

examples.ko: 반평생 동안 고향을 떠난 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I haven't left my hometown in half my life.
I heard they donated the money they had saved for half their life.

explain: 정확히 몇 년이라는 뜻보다 '아주 오랜 세월'이라는 느낌으로 써요. 어른이 자기 삶을 돌아보며 말할 때 자주 나와요. 평생 전체를 말할 때는 '평생'을 써요.

phrases.en: I've lived in this village for a good half of my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜 세월 살아온 삶을 돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking back on a long life lived.

phrases.example: 반평생 동안 한 가지 일만 했어요.
phrases.en: I did only one job for half my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴 기간을 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Marks a long period of time.

phrases.en: She devoted half her life to education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜 시간 한 가지에 힘썼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means devoting a long time to one thing.

explain_en: Half of one's life, often a long past stretch (할아버지는 반평생을 농사만 지으며 사셨어요.) It conveys 'a very long time' rather than an exact number of years, and adults often use it when looking back on their lives. For the whole of a life, use '평생'.

examples.en: When the power went out, we turned on the generator.
At the campsite they use a small generator.
The hospital has an emergency generator.
The generator is too noisy.
The wind turbine generator is spinning in the wind.
At the construction site they make electricity with a generator.

explain: 전기를 만들어 내는 기계예요. '발전소'는 전기를 만드는 큰 시설, '발전기'는 그 안이나 캠핑·공사장에서 쓰는 기계라는 점이 달라요. 소리가 같은 '발전기(發展期)'는 발전해 가는 시기를 뜻하니 문맥으로 구별하세요.

phrases.en: The power went out, so we ran the generator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 작동시켜 전기를 만든다는 뜻으로 '돌리다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '돌리다' is commonly used for running a machine to produce electricity.

phrases.en: The building has an emergency generator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정전에 대비해 준비해 두는 발전기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A generator kept ready for power outages.

phrases.en: The generator is too loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 돌아갈 때 나는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the noise a running generator makes.

explain_en: A machine that produces electricity. A '발전소' is a large power plant, while a 발전기 is the machine inside it or one used at campsites and construction sites. There is also a same-sounding 발전기 (發展期) meaning a period of development, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: The advance party leaves first and prepares the lodging.
Our team's advance group arrived in the morning.

examples.ko: 저는 선발대로 먼저 가서 자리를 잡을게요.
examples.en: I'll go ahead as the advance party and grab a spot.
Try contacting the advance group.

examples.ko: 등산 갈 때 선발대와 후발대로 나눴어요.
examples.en: For the hike, we split into an advance group and a rear group.

examples.ko: 행사 선발대에 뽑혀서 하루 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: I was chosen for the event's advance team, so I went a day early.

explain: 반대말은 '후발대'예요. 군대뿐 아니라 여행이나 행사에서 먼저 가서 준비하는 사람들에게도 써요. '선발'(뽑다)과 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 선발대의 '선'은 '먼저(先)'이고 선발(選拔)의 '선'은 '고르다'라서 한자가 달라요.

phrases.example: 저는 선발대로 먼저 가서 자리를 잡을게요.
phrases.en: I'll go first as the advance party and save seats.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로'를 붙여 먼저 가는 역할을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: -로 marks the role of going ahead first.
phrases.en_equiv: to go as the advance party

phrases.example: 행사 전날 선발대를 보내 장소를 확인했어요.
phrases.en: The day before the event, we sent an advance party to check the venue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비를 위해 사람들을 먼저 보낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means sending people ahead to prepare.

phrases.en: The advance party left, and the rear group left in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말이라서 함께 외우면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the opposite word, so it's good to learn together.

explain_en: The opposite is '후발대' (rear group). Besides the military, it is used for people who go ahead to prepare for trips or events. It is easy to confuse with '선발' (selection), but the '선' in 선발대 is 先 ('first'), while the '선' in 선발 is 選 ('choose'), so the Chinese characters differ.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 여타 가게보다 값이 싸요.
examples.en: This shop is cheaper than other shops.
We'll talk about the other issues tomorrow.
I'm good at English, but not at other foreign languages.
I'll tell you the remaining items separately.
The rest of the students have already gone home.
The rules are different in other cases.

explain: '여타'는 '그 밖의 나머지'를 말하고, 보통 명사 앞에서 '여타 + 명사'로 써요. '다른'보다 딱딱하고 글에 더 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '나머지'나 '다른'을 써도 충분해요.

phrases.en: This case is different from other cases.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여타'에 '의'를 붙여서 글에서 자연스럽게 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '여타' with '의' attached, a natural form in writing.

phrases.en: Let's talk about the other problems later.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여타'와 같은 뜻이고 더 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '여타' but softer.

phrases.en: The rest of the students went home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '여타' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요. 명사 앞뿐 아니라 혼자도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday substitute for '여타', and it can stand alone as a noun.

explain_en: Formal, written; things other than those mentioned (여타 자료) '여타' means 'everything else' and is usually placed before a noun: '여타 + noun'. It is stiffer than '다른' and appears more in writing. In everyday talk, '나머지' or '다른' work fine.

en: to be long; to be age-long

examples.en: Our country has a long history.

examples.ko: 이 바위는 장구한 세월 동안 바람을 맞았어요.
examples.en: This rock has been exposed to the wind for a very long time.
That tradition has continued for a very long time.
Since the history is long, there is a lot to see.
This temple's history is truly long.
The long-running debate finally ended.

explain: '길다'와 달리 시간, 역사, 세월처럼 오랜 기간에만 쓰는 글말이에요. '장구한 역사', '장구한 세월'처럼 앞에서 꾸며 주는 꼴로 가장 많이 써요. 악기 '장구'와는 소리만 같고 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 이 마을에는 장구한 전통이 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: This village still keeps a long tradition.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장구한 역사'처럼 오랜 기간 이어진 전통을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 장구한 역사, it describes a tradition that has lasted a very long time.

phrases.en: After a very long time, the rock became round.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긴 시간'보다 글말 느낌이 강하고 아주 오랜 기간을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More literary than 긴 시간, it means an extremely long period.

phrases.en: Gyeongju is a city proud of its long history.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장구한'이 가장 흔하게 붙는 짝말로, 오랜 역사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for 장구한, used when speaking of a long history.

explain_en: Formal or literary; very long history or time (장구한 역사). Unlike '길다' (long), it is a written-style word used only for long spans of time, such as history and years. It is most often used before a noun, as in '장구한 역사' and '장구한 세월'. It sounds the same as the drum '장구' but is a different word.

gh: long in length or in time
long in time only; for ages

p.n: 긴 is plain and ordinary; 장구한 sounds grand, literary, and ancient.

t90.ax: Our country has a long history.
